sections.title: Get to know your character
paragraphs: Type .cs in game to open your character sheet. Use .level or .xp to see your progression, and .xpbar to control the experience display.
Open .class to explore the available classes. Confirm only once you are happy with your choice: class selection is permanent. The Classes & talents guide explains the options.

sections.title: Find a first quest
paragraphs: Visit the Hunter’s Guildmaster in Britain for the original supply deliveries, monster bounties and expeditions. The expanding realm also adds town deliveries, hunts and walking escorts: use Quest givers around Felucca to find the planned contacts and the complete quest catalogue to compare their jobs.

Read an offer at its named NPC and choose Accept quest, then use the Quests button on your paperdoll to follow progress. The journal shows accepted jobs only. Choose Track for a compact display, and return to the issuing giver when the objectives are complete.
For a longer journey, seek the Grave Warden at Britain Graveyard to begin the seven stages of The Undying March. Check .achievements for milestones and .titles for unlocked overhead titles.

articles.summary: Find offers, follow your accepted quests, deliver supplies and guide an escort safely home.

sections.title: Find and accept a quest
paragraphs: The developing quest library contains 100 one-time contracts: 35 gathering and delivery jobs, 45 hunts and 20 escorts. The complete quest catalogue lists every objective and reward; the Quest givers guide lists the new town contacts and their planned locations.

Double-click a quest giver within three tiles to see their offers, read the story and choose Accept quest. At the Hunter’s Guildmaster, open Guild Quests from his panel first. Reading an offer does not accept it. The paperdoll’s Quests button shows only quests you have accepted and have not yet handed in.

The Hunter’s Guildmaster offers the original ten supply deliveries, ten bounties and ten expeditions, with one Guild journal contract active at a time. New town jobs and The Undying March are separate from that Guild slot. The rotating weekly quarry is a separate, repeatable activity.

sections.title: Read your journal and use Track
paragraphs: Select an accepted quest to see its issuing NPC, objectives, progress and rewards. Gathering, Hunts and Escorts filters help you find the job you need alongside the existing Guild categories.

Choose Track to open a compact live display for that quest. A supply job shows the first item still missing; a hunt shows the current stage and kill count; an escort shows its destination, coordinates and journey status.

The tracker is optional. Closing the journal keeps it closed until you open it again, and completed quests leave the active list. Hunt progress and completed escort arrival are saved; logging out interrupts a journey still in progress.

sections.title: Deliver supplies or complete a hunt
paragraphs: Supply jobs accept items you gather, craft, buy or already own. Carry every requested item in your backpack and return to the giver. A delivery with several requirements checks the full order before consuming anything; successful hand-in consumes the exact required quantities.

Hunts require kill credit from the combat system and the listed creature type. Player victims, pets, owned creatures, summons and invulnerable NPCs do not count. For an objective shown as several stages, finish each stage in order: later targets do not advance the quest early.

The Undying March begins with the Grave Warden at Britain Graveyard. Its seven stages lead from zombies and skeletons through ghouls, wraiths or spectres, liches and lich lords to an ancient lich. It pays 5,000 gold and 1,500 XP.

sections.title: Guide an escort on foot
paragraphs: Accepting an escort creates a walking companion for your character. Follow the destination shown in the journal and tracker, keep the companion close, and arrive together on Felucca. Only one walking escort can run per character.

A journey has a 30-minute limit. Staying more than 24 tiles apart for 10 seconds, changing facet, the death of you or your companion, or logging out interrupts it. Companions are vulnerable and carry no recoverable loot.

A failed journey stays in your journal. Return to its coordinator and choose Restart Escort to try again. Once your companion arrives safely, return to the issuing coordinator to collect payment; arriving alone does not finish the journey.

sections.title: Collect your reward or abandon a job
paragraphs: Return within three tiles of the issuing NPC when the objectives are complete. Gold and Guild Marks go into your backpack, with your bank used if no backpack is available. If a reward cannot be placed, it remains waiting: make room and return.

Each journal contract pays once per character. The catalogue’s XP rewards apply while character progression is enabled. Guild expeditions retain their Guild Marks, weekly scoring and achievement progress.

You may abandon an unfinished quest that is not ready for payment. This clears that quest’s progress and lets you accept it again from its giver. A completed or handed-in objective with a waiting reward is protected from abandonment.

sections.title: Weekly hunts and credit
paragraphs: Speak to the Hunter's Guildmaster within three tiles and accept the weekly quarry. Progress survives logout. Finish your current quarry and claim any pending reward before accepting another. After hand-in, the current weekly quarry can be accepted again.

A hunting week begins on Monday at 00:00 UTC. The quarry rotates through the eight entries below, and the reward modifier rotates through three entries independently. Qualifying hostile kills require at least 10% damage contribution; pets, summoned or protected creatures and civilians are excluded.
An accepted old-week quarry can still be completed for its saved reward and modifier. It cannot add points to the new week's board.

The Guild also offers ten one-time supply deliveries, ten bounties and ten expeditions through the quest journal. You may hold one of those Guild journal contracts at a time; the new town jobs are independent of that slot.

sections.title: The weekly top-ten board
paragraphs: The Guildmaster keeps current and previous weekly top-ten lists. Each handed-in weekly quarry adds its difficulty tier in points; Veteran's Hunt adds one more point.
Guild expeditions add their own tier in board points only if accepted and completed within the same week. Their one-time objectives and rewards are in the complete quest catalogue.

sections.title: Spending Marks and funding supplies
paragraphs: Carry Marks in your backpack and speak to the nearby Guildmaster. A purchase checks capacity before spending them.
You can donate 10,000 carried gold for one Mark, up to five donation Marks per week. Donations do not add hunting board points.

articles.title: Choosing a class and spending talents
articles.summary: Permanent class choice, talent points, rank caps, refunds and active-talent rules.

sections.title: Choose one of nine classes
paragraphs: Use .class to choose Druid, Hunter, Paladin, Warrior, Rogue, Warlock, Mage, Priest or Shaman. The confirmation menu makes this choice permanent for normal player use. These are custom character classes, separate from the classic skill-cap system.

Use .talents to allocate points. You earn floor(level / 2) points, capped at 50: first point at level 2, then one every two levels through level 100. Each class has five talents; each talent can reach rank 12. The full tree holds 60 ranks, so a 50-point character cannot maximize every talent.

Each + purchases one rank using one available point. Each − refunds one rank for 10,000 gold. Refunding all 12 ranks of one talent costs 120,000 gold. Refunding all 50 spent points costs 500,000 gold. Refunding points does not change your class.

sections.title: Use an active talent
paragraphs: Use .talentuse 1 through .talentuse 5 for the corresponding slot. Passive talents activate automatically once they have ranks. Active talents cost 5 + rank resource points: 6 at rank 1, 17 at rank 12. Warrior/Rogue actives and Hunter slots 1, 2 and 4 use stamina; the other active classes use mana. Talent costs do not list spell reagents.

Successful active talents share a 5-second recovery. Their effect duration can be much longer. Targeted talents require a living character within 12 tiles on the same facet. Healing/cleansing/ward talents restrict targets to yourself, your controlled pet, a party member or a party member’s controlled pet.

Area offensive talents select unowned NPCs. Cleave, Smoke Bomb and Storm Totem further require negative karma; Turn the Unhallowed uses its undead/demon classification. Curse of Agony also requires an eligible hostile creature in sight. Other targeted offensive talents retain their own checks, so normal combat and region rules still matter.

sections.title: Classes and spell schools
paragraphs: Warlock talents support Necromancy; Paladin talents support Chivalry. Their strength comes from spent talent ranks. There are no additional Necromancy or Chivalry skill gates, school multipliers or talent skill caps.

Learning a talent does not bypass a spell’s casting requirement. Necromancy controls casting checks and Spirit Speak supplies its spell power. Chivalry uses its own skill, positive karma and tithing points. Both schools have a base skill cap of 100.0 within the unchanged 1,200.0 total skill cap.

Warlock damage bonuses and Soul Leech apply to Pain Spike, Poison Strike, Strangle and Wither. Paladin Aura improves Close Wounds and Noble Sacrifice, and reduces Cleanse by Fire’s health cost. These talents do not add their school bonuses to Magery.

sections.title: Progress, claims and titles
paragraphs: Use .achievements to review progress and claim unlocked prizes. Use .titles to choose an unlocked overhead title, and .rewards for level milestones. Achievement progress is saved on your character.

Qualifying combat achievements use hostile, untamed, unsummoned creatures and at least 10% damage credit. Some milestones count distinct families or locations rather than repeated kills. Read the requirement column for each entry.

An entry's target is the number or threshold checked for its metric. Its points are achievement points, separate from XP. A named keepsake uses the listed base item with an achievement-specific name and hue.

Rewards are delivered in a bank parcel. If the bank lacks capacity, the claim stays available. Achievement notices remain until dismissed. Entries that reference currently inaccessible facets remain catalog objectives and do not unlock those facets.

articles.title: Pet levels & combat perks
articles.summary: Train a permanent companion to level 20 through meaningful combat, then choose its level 10 and level 20 perks.
articles.keywords: petlevel pet progression level experience xp taming companion bond hunter ferocious strikes iron hide siphoning bite apex predator adamant hide greater siphon transfer reset

sections.title: Inspect and train your pet
paragraphs: Type .petlevel and select one of your controlled pets on the same facet within 12 tiles. The training panel shows its level, accumulated experience, experience still needed and available special-skill choices.
Progression is enabled for owned controlled pets. Summoned and invulnerable creatures are excluded. Pets begin at level 1 and can reach level 20.

sections.title: Earn combat experience
paragraphs: A qualifying defeated enemy awards a base of 10 pet experience per difficulty point. Your pet must personally contribute at least 10% of all recorded damage, and its last recorded damage must be no more than 120 seconds old.

At the enemy’s death, both you and the pet must be on its facet and within 24 tiles of it; you must also be within 24 tiles of the pet and alive. Each pet that meets the threshold can receive its own reward. The reward is not divided among qualifying pets after that check.
Valid prey are wild combat NPCs. Civilians, guards, players, pets, summons, owned and invulnerable creatures do not qualify. Animal- and human-brained prey must have negative karma.

Weak prey give less experience as a pet grows. If enemy difficulty is below three times the pet’s level, the reward is quartered. Otherwise, if it is below five times the pet’s level, the reward is halved. More challenging prey give the full base reward, with whole-number rounding and a minimum award of 1.

rows: Half: below 5 × level but not below 3 × level

sections.title: Attributes and resource pools
paragraphs: Each level after level 1 adds 5 strength, dexterity and intelligence, and 5 to maximum health, stamina and mana. Level 10 therefore contributes +45 to each; level 20 contributes +95 to each.
A level gain also restores up to 5 current health, stamina and mana, capped at their new maxima. Merely initializing an existing pet at level 1 does not add a free stat bonus.

sections.title: Experience thresholds
paragraphs: Total experience to reach level N is 125 multiplied by the sum of the squares from 1 through N−1. Level 20 requires 308,750 total experience; the final step alone costs 45,125.

columns: XP from this level to the next
Bonus to each attribute and maximum pool

sections.title: Choose special skills
paragraphs: Choose one perk at level 10 and another at level 20. A chosen slot cannot be changed through the training panel. The two choices can be from the same or different families.

Matching attack choices add to +30% scripted melee damage; matching defensive choices add to 30% damage reduction. Matching siphon choices add to 30% healing from the adjusted hit damage, with the combined heal capped at 30 per hit.
Siphon applies when attacking NPCs that are not players and have no owner. It does not provide this heal from hitting another player’s pet. Healing is capped at the pet’s maximum health.

rows: Siphoning Bite: heal 10% of adjusted hit damage
Greater Siphon: heal 20% of adjusted hit damage
tables.caption: Siphon has a combined maximum of 30 health per hit, with a minimum heal of 1 when it applies.

sections.title: Hunter: Companion Bond
paragraphs: The Hunter’s Companion Bond talent adds 5% pet experience per rank and 1% pet melee damage per rank. At the configured 12-rank cap, that is +60% pet experience and +12% pet melee damage.

The experience bonus is applied after the weak-prey reduction. The damage bonus is combined with attack perks. It depends on the current owner’s Hunter talent, rather than being a permanent extra choice stored on the pet.

sections.title: Ownership changes reset training
paragraphs: Changing a pet’s owner resets its progression to level 1 and zero experience, clears both special-skill choices and removes its recorded progression bonuses. Its original base attributes and maximum pools are restored.
Plan a transfer before investing in long-term training. A trained pet’s progression belongs to that owner-and-pet partnership; it is not carried intact to the new owner.

articles.title: Combat rules and building a fighter
articles.summary: The shard uses custom Sphere combat with legacy armor, class talents and gathering-skill weapon bonuses.

sections.title: The rules in use
paragraphs: The shard enables 51 skills, including Necromancy and Chivalry, with 64 Magery, 17 Necromancy and 10 Chivalry spells alongside the nine-class talent system. Focus, Bushido, Ninjitsu, Spellweaving, Mysticism, Imbuing and Throwing remain disabled. Choosing a class is separate from learning and casting school spells.

Physical damage, hit checks and swing speed use the custom Sphere formulas. Armor uses a legacy armor rating rather than the later five-resistance percentage engine. Dexterity controls weapon timing. Stamina still matters for talent costs and the defender side of the custom hit check.
The tables describe the developing configuration and scripts. Native-engine formulas are source-derived expectations rather than a live damage benchmark.

sections.title: How a weapon hit is built
paragraphs: A weapon supplies its damage range. The custom player damage formula then adds a percentage based on Strength: by default floor(Strength × 10 / 100) percent, plus any applicable damage-increase property. The ordinary property contribution is capped between −100% and +100% before other bonuses. With Strength 100 and no other properties, a 15–19 weapon becomes a raw 16–20 range before later bonuses and defenses.

Unlike the selected alternative combat eras, the active native damage formula does not add an Anatomy or Tactics damage percentage. Tactics remains important to the custom attack/defense check. The shard separately adds its own gathering-skill and class bonuses.

Swordsmanship axes gain the Lumberjacking bonus; Macefighting weapons gain the Mining bonus. The gathering increase is applied first. Applicable class/party percentages are added together at the next stage. These custom percentage amounts round to the nearest integer, with positive halves rounded up. Armor, parry, damage-reduction talents, wards and other effects can lower the result.

sections.title: The custom hit check
paragraphs: The source model builds an attack value from effective weapon skill and effective Tactics, both measured in skill tenths: A = trunc((weapon skill + attacker Tactics) / 2). Its defense value is B = trunc((defender Tactics + current defender stamina × 10) / 2). If a melee attacker attacks a ranged-weapon defender, the stamina multiplier is 9 instead of 10.

It then calculates X = trunc((A − B) / 5), and D = clamp(trunc((weapon skill − X) / 10), 0, 100). A random difficulty from 0 through D − 1 feeds the combat success check; D = 0 uses zero. Sleeping or immobilized defenders instead use a random difficulty from 0 through 9. This is the selected engine routine, not the usual public-UO ratio of weapon skills.

For example, weapon skill 1000 and Tactics 1000 give A = 1000. Defender Tactics 1000 and stamina 100 give B = 1000 and D = 100. If that defender falls to stamina 20, B = 600 and D = 92. These values explain the inputs to the check; they are not measured live hit percentages. Weapon skill, Tactics and stamina are the relevant inputs here.

sections.title: A damage example
paragraphs: Suppose the native weapon roll is 20, your eligible gathering skill grants 30%, and your Warrior Weapon Forms plus Battle Cry grant 24% each. Gathering changes 20 to 26. The two class bonuses combine to 48%, adding round(26 × 48 / 100) = 12 for a raw hit of 38. This is an arithmetic example before armor, parry and target defenses; it is not a promise of 38 health lost on every attack.

Direct active talent damage is its own scripted attack. Cleaving Assault, Piercing Shot and similar fixed-rank attacks do not simply multiply the currently equipped weapon roll. Their listed amounts still enter the target’s damage handling.

articles.title: Weapon swing timers and archery
articles.summary: How Dexterity, weapon speed, movement, reach and ammunition affect attacks.

sections.title: Weapons with a speed rating
paragraphs: For a weapon with a nonzero speed rating S and adjusted Dexterity D, the source-derived full swing interval is max(0.5, floor(150000 / ((D + 100) × S)) / 10) seconds. The integer calculation rounds down to tenths of a second. Larger speed ratings mean faster weapons in this ruleset.

This formula uses adjusted Dexterity, including stat buffs, rather than your current stamina. Swing Speed Increase is not part of the selected custom timing formula. The engine splits the interval into recoil and the attack animation; the interval is not an extra wait to add after that animation.

sections.title: Unarmed and weapons without a speed
paragraphs: Unarmed combat and weapons with no speed rating use the fallback. Let B = floor((100 − adjusted Dexterity) × 40 / 100). If B is less than 5, use 5; otherwise add 5. Unarmed combat then adds 2 tenths of a second. At Dexterity 100, the expected unarmed interval is 0.7 seconds; at Dexterity 50 it is 2.7 seconds.

An unrated weapon adds its weight modifier instead: floor(weight in stones × 10 / 4) tenths. A two-handed unrated weapon also adds half of the pre-weight interval. This weight fallback does not apply when the weapon already supplies a nonzero speed rating.

sections.title: Ranged positioning and ammunition
paragraphs: Normal Archery requires ammunition and does not allow moving fire. After your last movement, stand still for at least 1 second before a new ranged attack starts. A shield prevents a ranged attack. Two-handed bows normally occupy the second hand.

Weapon-specific range overrides the global 2–15-tile default. Standard bow: 2–10 tiles, arrows, damage 15–19, speed 29. Standard crossbow: 2–8 tiles, bolts, damage 18–22, speed 26. Standard heavy crossbow: 2–8 tiles, bolts, damage 20–24, speed 20. These base definitions can differ from crafted, magic or named variants.

At Dexterity 100 the expected standard bow interval is 2.5 seconds, crossbow 2.8 seconds and heavy crossbow 3.7 seconds. The movement requirement is a condition for starting the shot, not a damage bonus.

Native ranged attacks check line of sight and range. Piercing Shot is a separate active talent: it requires an equipped Archery weapon and a living target from 2 through 12 tiles on the same facet. It deals its talent amount rather than the standard weapon damage roll.

articles.title: Armor, parrying and Magic Resistance
articles.summary: Legacy armor, equipment-based blocking, spell resistance and the order of defensive talents.

sections.title: Legacy armor rating
paragraphs: Displayed armor is a weighted rating over body coverage. With armor stacking disabled, the strongest armor covering a region counts for that region; several overlapping pieces do not automatically add all their ratings. Protection contributes its effect directly to the rating.

Armor produces a randomized damage deduction rather than a flat percentage equal to displayed armor. In the available native source, magic-tagged damage halves that deduction. Magic is not globally configured to ignore armor. Fire immunity can separately stop fire-tagged damage.

For total native armor rating A, the source draws an integer Q from 7 through 34 and calculates M = floor(A × Q / 100). The ordinary deduction is floor(M / 2), with a possible extra point when M is odd; magic-tagged damage then halves that deduction, rounding down. For total AR 50, the source-model deduction is 1–8 from an ordinary hit, or 0–4 from magic-tagged damage. Fixed/bypass damage is handled separately.

The elemental-resistance percentage engine is disabled. A fire/cold/poison/energy label still matters to immunity and scripted checks, but it does not enable the later five-resistance damage formula. Native Slayer combat is also disabled in the configured combat flags; do not assume a Slayer property grants its expansion-era multiplier.

sections.title: Parrying
paragraphs: Shields and two-handed weapons may parry. A lone one-handed weapon cannot parry under the selected flags. Shield parry chance is floor(raw Parrying skill in tenths / 40); two-handed weapon chance is floor(raw Parrying / 80). At 100.0 Parrying, a positive chance gains 5 percentage points.

If adjusted Dexterity is below 80, multiply the chance by (20 + Dexterity) / 100 and round down. At Dexterity 80 or higher, there is no low-Dexterity reduction. A successful ordinary parry blocks the whole weapon hit; no alternate partial-block effect is configured on the Parrying skill.

sections.title: Resisting a spell
paragraphs: Only spells marked resistible make this check. A successful native resistance roll reduces damage by 25%; it is not a universal Magic Resistance percentage subtracted from every spell. The expected native chance uses base Magic Resistance and caster Magery, and is documented here as a source-derived rule.

Let R be floor(base Magic Resistance), M be caster base Magery in tenths, and n the spell number. A = floor(R / 5). B = max(0, R − (trunc((M − 200) / 50) + 50 × (1 + floor(n / 8)))). The nominal resistance chance is max(A, B) percent. The native random comparison can include a small endpoint difference.

For 100.0 Magic Resistance against a 100.0 Magery caster’s Fireball (spell 18), A is 20 and B is 0, giving a nominal 20% resistance roll. If the unmitigated effect is 16, resistance alone subtracts floor(16 × 25 / 100) = 4. Armor and class defenses follow their own stages.

Heal and Greater Heal are not damaging resistible spells. Mana Drain and Mana Vampire carry resistible flags, but their legacy mana handling is a separate native effect; do not equate the 25% damage reduction with a guaranteed reduction in mana removed.

sections.title: Class defenses and wards
paragraphs: Applicable class and party damage-reduction percentages add together, with a 75% cap at this stage. Barkskin/Owlbear and Shield Wall require physical-tagged damage. Last Stand works while health is at or below round(30% of maximum), using the nearest whole-health threshold. Ancestral Guardian contributes to the same sum.

After the percentage reduction, a Divine Bulwark ward absorbs remaining damage from its point pool. Prismatic Ward can then spend 2 mana per further point absorbed, limited by talent rank, remaining damage and available mana. Guardian Angel checks the resulting hit for lethality and can leave its Priest at 1 health while cancelling that hit.

Rogue Evasion can return zero for a physical hit before the percentage/ward stages. Direct damage, weapons and spell attacks may carry different physical/magic flags, so check the attack type rather than assuming every effect uses the same defense.

articles.title: Magery casting, damage and healing
articles.summary: The enabled spellbook, reagents, casting times, potency curves, interruption and spell stacking.

sections.title: Casting a spell
paragraphs: Normal spellbook casting requires the spell in your book, the listed Magery requirement, enough mana and one of each listed reagent unless a quantity is explicitly shown. Scrolls and wands use their native item rules. Scroll casting uses half the normal mana cost and half the normal skill difficulty; charged wands cost no mana and consume a charge. Item spell strength can differ from your own Magery.

Casting while holding equipment is enabled. Players speak the configured words of power. Precasting and freeze-on-cast are not enabled. The normal spell target must satisfy native visibility, line-of-sight, facet and anti-magic checks.

Aborting or failing a cast is configured to lose neither mana nor reagents. Successful casts still consume their costs. All 64 Magery spells have a 100% configured interruption curve: an eligible incoming hit can interrupt casting. Protection’s expansion-style interruption prevention is tied to the disabled elemental engine, so do not rely on it as guaranteed uninterrupted casting here.

Mage Quick Incantation subtracts 0.1 seconds per rank, with a 0.1-second minimum cast time. Any Faster Casting property handled by the native engine subtracts 0.2 seconds per point before the class adjustment. No general class talent recovery is imposed on ordinary Magery casts.

sections.title: Reading the effect and duration tables
paragraphs: The effect columns list configured curve endpoints at 0 and 100 spell potency. They are not the minimum and maximum damage of a Grandmaster cast. The source model obtains adjusted Magery, randomizes direct target potency to roughly half through just below its full value, and then interpolates the spell’s effect curve.

For a two-endpoint curve low → high and potency P in tenths, expected effect = low + round((high − low) × P / 1000). The native interpolation rounds to the nearest integer; half values round away from zero. A single value stays constant. Adjusted skills can slightly exceed their base cap due to stats or modifiers, and the native curve can extrapolate beyond its listed 100-potency endpoint.

At an exact input potency of 100.0 before randomization, Heal’s 5 → 20 curve gives 13–20 health and Greater Heal’s 10 → 50 curve gives 30–50, before any other effect changes. The typical adjusted Magery input differs from exact 100.0; these are explanatory source-model examples, not measured live ranges.

Normal cast durations are calculated from cast potency before the direct target randomization. The duration columns show the configured 0 → 100 potency curve in seconds. Poison uses a native pulse lifecycle instead of treating its printed duration as a simple poison expiry.

sections.title: Skill and stat scaling
paragraphs: The selected magic flags do not enable the later OSI spell formula. Therefore its Evaluating Intelligence multiplier, Intelligence damage-increase percentage and Inscription damage bonus are not automatically part of ordinary spell damage. Magery’s native adjusted-skill bonus does include its configured Intelligence contribution, explained under Skills and Stats.

Magic Arrow and Harm are configured as physical + magic damage. Fireball, Fire Field and Flamestrike are fire + magic; Lightning, Energy Bolt and Chain Lightning are energy + magic; Mind Blast is cold + magic; Meteor Swarm and Earthquake are physical + magic; Explosion uses general + magic. These classifications differ from some public UO guides.

Applicable class spell-power bonuses increase the native health effect before later resistance, armor and target defenses. Separate percentage bonuses such as the two Mage damage talents apply in sequence, each rounding its added amount to the nearest integer with positive halves rounded up. Direct talent heals such as Lay on Hands and Prayer of Restoration have independent formulas; both these direct heals and native class spell effects were verified in isolated tests.

Warlock talents support Necromancy, and Paladin Aura supports Chivalry. They do not add their school damage or healing bonuses to Magery. Necromancy’s Spirit Speak formulas and Chivalry’s karma and tithing rules are explained in their own guides.

sections.title: Buffs, reflection and disruption
paragraphs: Different stat spells share the stat-effect slot with stat stacking disabled. A new stat spell normally replaces the old effect instead of keeping simultaneous Strength, Agility, Cunning, Bless and Curse effects together. Separate effects such as Night Sight have their own slots.

Magic Reflection is consumed by a reflectable hostile direct spell. If both participants have reflection, the native source consumes both effects and can send the effect back to the original target. Harmful self-casting is disabled unless native reflection creates the return path.

Damage normally breaks paralysis/root immobilization and can interrupt a magic action, unless the attack’s flags explicitly prevent those effects. Talent roots use the same immobilization flag. Poison pulses are marked not to disturb casting. Purification directly cures poison and clears immobilization; it is an active Priest talent rather than a resistance roll.

sections.title: Poison strength and pulses
paragraphs: Poison spells and poisoned weapons use the enabled legacy model. Poison strength is a value from 0 through approximately 1000, rather than the later fixed-level OSI formula. Normal Poison’s effect curve is 100 → 750; Poison Field’s is 50 → 500.

The source lifecycle starts its first pulse after 1–2 seconds. Later pulses occur every 5–8 seconds. Each pulse lowers stored poison strength by 50. Initial pulse charges are floor(strength / 50) for spell-applied poison. The effect stops when charges/strength are exhausted or a cure removes it.

The native pulse chooses a tier from the strength before reducing it. Its damage is the greater of the tier minimum and floor(maximum health × tier × 2 / 100), before normal magic/poison damage handling. Poison pulses do not disturb casting.

sections.title: Cure, Arch Cure and bandages
paragraphs: In the selected model, cure chance follows the native skill-success curve for cure potency minus remaining poison strength, with a 10.0-potency variance. Equal strength gives approximately 50%; being 10.0 potency above gives approximately 75%, and being 10.0 below gives approximately 25%. This is not the expansion potion-tier cure table.

Cure targets one character. Arch Cure applies the cure to an area within 2 tiles. Healing/Veterinary bandages treat poison before ordinary health restoration, so a successful poison treatment does not also produce their ordinary wound heal. Priest Purification directly removes poison and immobilization from a valid ally.

Poisoned native weapons can deliver poison and lose their remaining poison strength on hits. Venomcraft is a separate Rogue proc and uses its own rank-based chance. Ordinary weapon poison delivery and Rogue Venomcraft are distinct checks.

paragraphs: Pain Spike, Poison Strike, Strangle and Wither qualify for the damage talents. Their power still depends on Spirit Speak. Magery and other spell schools do not trigger Soul Leech, receive these damage bonuses or consume Life for Power.

Agony, Pact Familiar and Life for Power apply their bonuses in that order, each with integer rounding. The percentages multiply in sequence. Damage and healing remain subject to normal combat defenses and maximum health.

Soul Leech works with direct hits and timed pulses. It excludes players, owned pets, summons, protected creatures and self damage. Tiny hits can round to zero healing; there is no guaranteed one-point heal.

Life for Power lasts until a qualifying positive Necromancy effect. Pain Spike and Strangle consume it on their first positive pulse. The first qualifying target of an area effect consumes the charge. You must have more health than the rounded sacrifice plus one before using it.

Dread Presence recognizes your own active curse. Another Warlock’s curse provides no protection for you, and an expired, dispelled or removed curse stops granting the reduction.

The cat-shaped shadow familiar is separate from Necromancy’s Dark Wolf Familiar. Its damage bonus requires your own living controlled familiar on the same facet within 12 tiles. Death, removal, transfer, distance or the two-minute expiry removes that bonus.

articles.title: Party buffs, roots, curses and wards
articles.summary: Who receives party support, how shared buffs stack, and when timed effects end.

sections.title: Who receives party effects
paragraphs: Without a party, group support applies to you. In a party, the script examines up to ten members. Recipients must be alive, on the same facet and within 12 tiles when the effect is applied. Summoned pets are not extra recipients in the party-member loop.

Targeted healing/ward/cleansing talents allow yourself, your pet, a party member or a party member’s pet. They require the ordinary 12-tile/same-facet/live-target check. Party-area casts and targeted ally casts therefore have different recipient sets.

sections.title: Stacking and refreshing
paragraphs: Wild Renewal, Renewing Prayer and Healing Rain share one healing-over-time amount and timer generation per target. Reapplying one replaces the existing amount and resets five pulses; it does not create an additional independent stack. Each pulse caps at current maximum health.

Battle Cry and Ancestral Guardian each retain the stronger of their current and newly supplied values while refreshing their own generation/expiry. Divine Bulwark adds its new absorb points to the current pool and refreshes a 30-second expiration. Ward absorption consumes points as damage arrives.

Talent roots likewise use a generation marker. The latest root owns the expiration callback, and a stale callback cannot clear a newer root. Native paralysis and the talent root share immobilization state; damaging/disruptive effects and Purification can free a target.

sections.title: Effect limits and lifecycle
paragraphs: Damage-reduction percentages combine with a 75% cap. The ward pool and Prismatic Ward then absorb remaining damage separately. Healing cannot exceed maximum health and does not turn a dead character into a living one.

Owlbear Shape and Pact Familiar are explicitly cleaned up at logout; Owlbear is also restored at login. Storm pulses use client-bound state and stop when disconnected. Persistent timer generations prevent an old callback from acting on a new effect after reconnect. These lifecycle rules do not grant an extra duration extension.

articles.title: Character levels and experience
articles.summary: The 100-level XP curve, damage shares, pet-owner credit and talent points.

sections.title: Level curve and commands
paragraphs: Use .xp or .level to see total XP, current level and XP remaining. Use .cs or .charactersheet for the overview. Level 1 starts at zero. Maximum level is 100 and maximum stored XP is 495,000.

Cumulative XP to reach level L is 50 × L × (L − 1). Going from level L to L + 1 costs 100 × L XP. Levels do not directly grant stat points or raise the base skill caps in these scripts; their class benefit is the talent-point schedule.

Earned talent points are floor(level / 2), capped at 50. Character XP is stored persistently. The player death hook does not subtract this custom XP; death can still have separate native fame/item consequences.

sections.title: Monster XP and contribution shares
paragraphs: An eligible victim’s base XP pool is max(1, floor((2 × original Strength + original Dexterity + original Intelligence) / 10)), capped by the script’s safety limits. Current wounds and temporary stat effects are not used. A creature with original STR 100, DEX 100 and INT 100 supplies 40 XP before shares.

Victims must be eligible wild NPCs: animal, monster or dragon brains, or a negative-Karma human-brain opponent. Player characters, pets, owned creatures, conjured creatures, invulnerable creatures and explicitly excluded/already-paid victims do not produce this ordinary hunt payout.

Each recipient receives floor(pool × credited damage / all recorded victim damage). All damage in the native attacker ledger counts in the denominator, even damage from attackers who cannot collect. Your controlled pet’s eligible damage is credited to you and combined with your own contribution.

At payout, a credited player must be alive, on the same facet and within 24 tiles. Its eligible attacker entry must be no more than 120 seconds old. Having a party does not automatically split this particular pool evenly: actual ledger damage and pet ownership determine the share.

Hunter Trailblazer adds 5% per rank to this hunt share, rounding its bonus to the nearest integer after the initial share rounds down. The achievement/Hunter’s Guild kill-credit check requires your combined credited contribution to reach at least 10% of all recorded damage. This 10% test is separate from receiving a smaller positive XP share.

sections.title: Examples
paragraphs: A 40-XP creature takes 75% of its recorded damage from you and 25% from another eligible player. The ordinary shares are 30 and 10 XP. If you have rank-12 Trailblazer, your 30 is increased by 60% to 48. Integer rounding can leave a remainder undistributed.

If your pet deals 40% and you deal 20%, your owner credit is 60%. On a 100-XP victim your share is 60, subject to range/alive/age checks. A teammate who dealt no recorded damage receives no automatic share merely for party membership.
Quest and achievement reward XP comes from their own reward scripts. Trailblazer’s hunt multiplier does not automatically multiply all those independent rewards.

articles.title: All 51 skills, stat caps and effective skill
articles.summary: The 49 classic skills plus Necromancy and Chivalry, their caps and configured stat contributions.

sections.title: Caps and training
paragraphs: The default player skill class allows 100.0 in each of 51 enabled skills: the 49 classic skills plus Necromancy and Chivalry. The total cap remains 1,200.0 skill points. Base Strength, Dexterity and Intelligence each cap at 100, with 300 total. Temporary buffs and equipment can change adjusted values without changing these base training limits.

The custom RPG class choice does not replace this default skill class. Level 100 does not automatically give skills over 100.0. Use the skill locks to manage what can rise or fall as you approach the total cap.

NPC training costs 1 gold per 0.1 skill. A trainer can teach no higher than the smaller of 42.0 and 30% of that NPC’s own skill. Training dummies/archery practice devices stop at their configured 30.0 practice limit. Unchosen starting skills are capped at 20.0 during creation; this is not a permanent trained-skill cap.

Necromancy controls its school’s casting checks, while Spirit Speak supplies spell power. Chivalry uses its own skill, positive karma and tithing points. The Necromancer and Paladin character-creation presets include these schools; Paladin uses Meditation instead of the disabled Focus skill. Focus, Bushido, Ninjitsu, Spellweaving, Mysticism, Imbuing and Throwing remain disabled.

sections.title: Base skill versus effective skill
paragraphs: Some native checks use base skill, others use adjusted/effective skill. The configured stat contribution is: raw bonus in skill tenths = floor(B × (Ws × adjusted STR + Wd × adjusted DEX + Wi × adjusted INT) / 10000). B is the “stat factor” below; Ws/Wd/Wi are the listed Strength/Dexterity/Intelligence weights. Divide the raw result by ten to express displayed skill points.

For Magery, weights are 0/0/100 and factor 15. At Intelligence 100 the raw bonus is 15, or 1.5 skill points. Base Magery 100.0 therefore supplies expected effective Magery 101.5 before any other skill modifier. Weapon skills with factor 10 and equally weighted combined stats of 100 receive 1.0 effective point.
The last column assumes all three adjusted stats are 100 and no other skill modifiers. It is a contribution to checks that use effective skill, not a new permanent skill-cap increase.

sections.title: Success chances and skill gain
paragraphs: Ordinary skill checks compare effective skill against the action’s difficulty on the native success curve. At equal skill/difficulty the source curve is about 50%; 10.0 skill above is about 75%, 20.0 above about 87.5%; the inverse differences give about 25% and 12.5%. Particular actions can set random or recipe-specific difficulty and can have additional gates.

Combat does not use that ordinary success curve: the selected custom hit routine builds a difficulty from attacker weapon skill/Tactics and defender Tactics/current stamina, then uses native random checks. Skill gain uses separate advance curves and cap/lock checks. A skill’s action delay or recipe requirement is not a guarantee of gain on every attempt.

The enabled Enticement path is the classic lure action in the available native source. Spell files for expansion bard effects are inactive, so do not assume modern Discordance debuffs from the client’s label alone.

articles.title: Healing, regeneration and death
articles.summary: Bandages, Meditation, natural recovery, resurrection health and custom XP preservation.

sections.title: Vitals and baseline recovery
paragraphs: Maximum health normally follows adjusted Strength, stamina follows adjusted Dexterity and mana follows adjusted Intelligence, unless a creature/item/effect supplies an explicit maximum or modifier. The current values shown in your character sheet can be below those maxima.

The configured baseline natural recovery intervals are one health every 40 seconds, one mana every 20 seconds and one stamina every 10 seconds. Character-specific regeneration properties/effects can alter these rates or amounts. Food decays on the configured one-day interval. Human/Elf/Gargoyle racial regeneration bonuses are not enabled.

Active Meditation uses a configured 2.0 → 1.0-second delay curve. In the available native source it restores one mana per successful meditation pulse when no alternate skill effect is supplied, continuing until mana is full. Movement is not configured to abort Meditation. The separate equipment-linked meditation helper is not documented as a guaranteed passive OSI regeneration bonus.

sections.title: Bandages
paragraphs: Healing uses a 3.0 → 1.0-second action delay and a source-model effect curve of 20 → 200 health at 0 → 100 effective Healing. Veterinary has a fixed 2.0-second delay and no explicit alternative effect curve in its skill definition; the available native source uses a 1-health fallback for an ordinary successful wound heal. The target must remain touchable and within 2 tiles.

The native bandage action prioritizes resurrection, then poison treatment, then ordinary wound healing. It consumes a bandage on the processed success/failure paths. Native starting difficulty is random 0–79 for ordinary healing, 50–99 for a poisoned target and 85–109 for a dead target/corpse, before the ordinary skill-success check. These are source-derived action rules, not fixed minimum-skill promises.

For ordinary Healing, the available source initializes the action effect from the configured curve at effective skill, then uses that amount on successful healing, capped by maximum health. No automatic Anatomy bonus is shown in this active bandage implementation. Cure success instead uses healing/veterinary potency versus the remaining poison strength.

sections.title: Death and resurrection
paragraphs: Resurrection returns 10% of maximum health, with a minimum of 1. The Magery Resurrection spell is circle 8, costs 50 mana, requires 80.0 Magery and has a 2.3-second base cast. Native anti-magic and valid-dead-target checks apply.

Custom character XP and its derived level are not subtracted by the deployed player death hooks. Native fame loss and corpse/item rules are separate; the available source reduces player fame by one tenth unless a character override prevents it.

Dead characters are configured not to see living characters normally. The character sheet records deaths, and resurrection may restore a matching reachable corpse’s contents through native corpse handling. Guardian Angel prevents one incoming lethal hit while available; it does not substitute for resurrecting a character who is already dead.

sections.title: Decode and locate the treasure
paragraphs: Treasure maps are configured for Felucca. Maps created on disabled facets fall back to Felucca. The map level controls both the Cartography requirement and the chest lock difficulty.
Double-click an undecoded map to decode it once your Cartography meets its level requirement. Digging also checks your Cartography, so borrowing a decoded map does not bypass the required skill.

Once decoded, a level 1–5 treasure map shows its exact X, Y and Z coordinates in the item details. The matching development client also shows a coordinate footer below the opened map. Ordinary and undecoded maps do not display that footer.
The Lockpicking column records the configured lock setting. It is not a guaranteed success threshold: the supplied engine evaluates a native lock difficulty and skill check.

sections.title: Digging rules
paragraphs: Equip a pickaxe and stand beside the marked location on the correct facet. Flying characters cannot dig. The excavation advances through 25 one-second steps; moving or unequipping the pickaxe interrupts it. The treasure cannot be raised while you stand directly on its tile.
The location must be on suitable outdoor dirt, grass, forest, jungle, sand or snow. Guarded, safe and underground regions, occupied multis and nearby trees, rocks or walls can block excavation.
Mining widens the distance at which you can find the treasure; it does not replace the map's Cartography requirement.

sections.title: Chest contents by level
paragraphs: Every completed excavation creates a locked chest and reveals the digger. Reagent entries independently choose a random reagent and a stack of 40–60. Equipment entries independently choose equally among a normal weapon, European armor, clothing or a Magery scroll; the table counts rolls, so repeated types are possible.
The combination-stone chance is one extra roll per chest: 1 in 10,000 on level 4, and 1 in 1,000 on level 5. Levels 1–3 do not roll it.

sections.title: Guardians and chest removal
paragraphs: Guardians spawn near the chest, keep an eight-tile home range and have a one-hour removal timer. The treasure chest also has a one-hour decay timer.
The player who dug up the chest can remove it when it is visible and within line of sight. Removing a chest destroys anything left inside; collect the contents first.

sections.title: Opening dungeon chests
paragraphs: Dungeon chests begin locked and have a one-hour decay timer. The Unlock spell is explicitly blocked on these chests. After an unlocked dungeon chest is double-clicked, its timer is reset to three minutes.
Loot tables below list independent rolls; for example, three rolls at 1 in 3 can produce zero, one, two or three results. These are dungeon chest rewards, separate from treasure-map chests.

paragraphs: Gold stack: 30–100. This chest can carry a dart, explosion or poison trap.

sections.title: Chest level 2

paragraphs: Gold stack: 200–400. This definition does not add a trap when created.

sections.title: What container traps actually do
paragraphs: A trap fires once when an unlocked container is opened, then removes itself. A locked container does not spring its trap until it can open. Dart traps deal physical damage, explosion traps deal fire damage, and poison traps deal poison-type damage equal to their stored trap strength.

Telekinesis from more than two tiles away is recognized by the trap script and sets direct trap damage to zero. The script's poison branch applies poison-type damage; it does not call a lasting poison effect.

paragraphs: Type .reputation to review persistent scores. Each track starts at zero and is bounded between −1,000 and +1,000. City, race and alignment scores are separate.

sections.title: Faction behavior
paragraphs: Assigned faction guards can react aggressively to players below −250 on their faction's track. Hostile faction shopkeepers refuse service. NPC placement and assigned faction determine which track applies.

sections.title: Faction shop prices
paragraphs: Positive reputation gives a linear discount, rounded down: score × 30 / 1,000 percent. Scores at zero or below receive no discount; +1,000 gives the maximum 30%. Price is then rounded down after applying that discount, with a minimum of one gold.

sections.title: Using Mining
paragraphs: Mining has a 1.6-second configured skill delay and a two-tile targeting range. Dismount before mining. The equipped tool needs charges; each successful Mining action spends one charge and destroys the tool when its last charge is used.

Resource skill ranges below are the gathering resource's configured difficulty range, not a promised success percentage. Smelting uses the ore item's separate Mining requirement. The optional custom OSI smelting formula is disabled, so native smelting applies.

sections.title: Every ore tier
paragraphs: Default resource weights are relative selection weights, not direct drop percentages. The default rock pool also has weight 10 for no resource and 0.1 for diamond. Shadow ore is available in dungeon and spooky pools rather than the default surface pool.
Mytheril and Mithril are separate material names in this library. Blackrock harvesting is set to 99.9–100.0 Mining and its smelting requirement is 100.0.

sections.title: Regional differences and regeneration
paragraphs: Default rock uses the material weights shown above. Dungeon rock uses weights 100 nothing, 30 iron and 5 shadow; spooky rock uses 65 nothing, 30 iron and 5 shadow; swamp rock has only nothing. Actual regional resource events control which pool applies.

sections.title: Gathering logs
paragraphs: Lumberjacking has a 1.6-second configured delay and a two-tile targeting range. A charged equipped tool is required; each successful action consumes one charge and destroys an exhausted tool.

Wood nodes yield 1–3 logs per successful harvest and regenerate after ten hours. The default tree pool has weight 60 for no resource plus the relative wood weights below. Weights are not independent percentages.

Damage values are the specialty weapon definition's base range; final combat damage also depends on character skills, stats and other combat effects. A dash indicates that this custom tier does not define that weapon here.

sections.title: Fishing rules
paragraphs: Fishing has an eight-second configured skill delay and a four-tile targeting range. You cannot fish while mounted; that restriction is checked both at the start and while fishing. Successful catches are placed in your backpack.

The default water pool has relative weights 60 for nothing and 10 each for four big-fish variants. Each fish resource has a 1.0–100.0 skill range, a node amount of 9–30 and a per-harvest amount of 1–3. Fishing nodes regenerate after ten hours.
These weights describe the active default gathering pool, not a 40% success guarantee for every cast. Your skill and local resource state also affect outcomes.

sections.title: Using your catch
paragraphs: Fish is used in cooking and the Fresh Fish supply contract requires 20 raw fish steaks. Boats provide access to ocean water; their movement commands are in Boats & sailing.
The active Fishing skill does not contain a custom SOS, shipwreck, sea-monster or fishing-net reward override. Item definitions alone are not evidence of an enabled custom fishing reward system.

sections.title: Grandmaster recipe discoveries
paragraphs: A confirmed successful catch at real/base Fishing 100.0 or higher has a 0.2% chance (1 in 500) to award one custom recipe scroll. Bonuses cannot qualify a character whose base Fishing is below 100.0.

All eight Wayfarer’s Verse Bard recipes can appear with equal selection weight. Failed, empty or cancelled catches do not roll, and a single catch can award at most one scroll. Each eligible catch is independent; a scroll is not guaranteed by the 500th catch.

Learn a scroll from your backpack to unlock its Tailoring piece permanently on that character, or trade it to another player. See Custom recipe discoveries for the complete costs and other drop sources.

Owners and co-owners can secure containers. Friends can lock down items, and can release their own lockdowns. Owner, co-owner and friend checks are repeated when a target action is completed, and the target must still belong to the same house.

sections.title: Buying and selling
paragraphs: The owner can put a house up for sale through its sign with a positive numeric price, or take it off the market. A buyer must reopen the sign if the owner, price or listing changes before confirming.

Purchases recheck the current owner and buyer eligibility, transfer the property, then charge the sale price. A failed transfer does not charge gold. Review the displayed sale price and sign information before accepting.

Owners can separately offer full ownership to another character. Accepting a transfer changes the owner and updates house ownership counts. House and native account eligibility can prevent a transfer.

sections.title: Static-property storage upgrades
paragraphs: The +25% storage option for a static property uses one-eighth of its property value and grants the selected +25% storage. The corrected selection keeps this option from being mistaken for a different upgrade. For a property valued at 80,000 gold, this option costs 10,000 gold.

sections.title: Redeeding and demolition
paragraphs: The configured redeeding fee is 10% of the applicable property value, and the demolition fee is 5%. Purchased storage and construction enter the relevant value/refund calculations; the confirmation dialog shows the resulting terms for that property type.

The housing setting crates house items when redeeding. Review the confirmation and collect or secure your contents before removing a house. The exact refund flow differs for classic houses, custom foundations and static properties.

sections.title: Using and timing potions
paragraphs: Ordinary drunk potions use a shared 15-second reuse timer in the supplied engine source. The potion definitions here do not override that delay. You cannot drink another ordinary potion while its reuse marker remains active. Shrink potions use their own scripted pet-target interaction, and explosion potions use the throw interaction.

The numerical effect ranges below are calculated from active item and spell definitions plus the supplied engine source. They are a source model, not a measurement from the running server. An ordinary potion randomizes its strength to roughly half through just below full strength before evaluating its spell curve; healing and restoration are limited by missing HP, mana or stamina. These amounts assume no Enhance Potions bonus or other alteration to stored potion strength.

Strength in the table is the stored potion strength, not a minimum skill needed to use it. Alchemy skills and ingredients are in the complete Alchemy recipes. Lasting stat, Night Sight and Invisibility potion effects share a native potion-effect slot, so do not assume different lasting potions stack.

sections.title: Explosion potions
paragraphs: The supplied engine uses a default four-second countdown after igniting an explosion potion. A throw target must pass line-of-sight and wall checks. The explosion has a two-tile radius and fire damage.

Unlike ordinary drinking, the explosion item evaluates the Explosion spell's effect at full stored potion strength before creating the blast. The listed Lesser, normal and Greater Explosion amounts are therefore 25, 31 and 41 base damage in this source model, before target protection and other damage processing. Do not keep an ignited potion in hand while its countdown expires.

sections.title: Cure and poison
paragraphs: The current Pre-AOS cure model compares cure strength with the active poison strength through the native success curve. The potion's applied strength is randomized, so a named cure tier is not a guaranteed cure of every poison. Poison potions use the Poison effect and are also inputs for the Poisoning skill.

sections.title: Potion kegs
paragraphs: A keg stores up to 100 potions of one matching base potion type. Double-click it and target a potion to fill it, or target an empty bottle in your backpack to draw one out. Different potion types cannot be mixed.

The keg stores the average strength of the added potions and restores that strength when bottling. An empty keg cannot fill a bottle. The crafted keg requires Tinkering 65.0, eight boards, one barrel tap and one barrel hoop.

sections.title: Cooking and eating

sections.title: Joining an invasion
paragraphs: The automatic scheduler is enabled by default and chooses a new event delay between three and five hours. Staff can change that setting, so watch the realm announcements for the active event. Only one invasion runs at a time.

A forming invasion announces its location two minutes before wave one. At least one living player must be within 36 tiles on Felucca when that preparation ends. The event uses up to ten nearby players to size its waves; this is a scaling limit rather than a ten-player entry restriction.

sections.title: Wave sizes and timing
paragraphs: Four regular waves are followed by a boss wave. There is a twenty-second pause after each cleared regular wave. A wave that remains alive for five minutes ends the invasion without completion rewards; the whole event has a thirty-minute limit.

Regular wave size is 2 + site tier + floor(nearby players / 3) + wave number, clamped to 3–8 creatures. The final wave contains its boss plus 1 + floor(nearby players / 3) adds, clamped to 2–5 adds. Nearby player count is measured when the invasion begins.

sections.title: Contribution and rewards
paragraphs: Defeat every wave to qualify for completion rewards. Your recorded damage must reach at least 2% of the combined maximum health of creatures spawned across the invasion; this earns one Hunter’s Guild Mark. At least 10% earns two Marks. Creature corpse loot is separate.

Damage credit requires the player to be alive, online, on Felucca and within 55 tiles of the event controller when it is recorded. Up to 32 participants are tracked. Earned Marks are claimed automatically when possible; use .waveclaim to collect saved Marks after making room in your backpack. Up to twenty unclaimed Marks can be held.

sections.title: Enchanting a weapon
paragraphs: Put a Magi Stone, an Amplifier Stone and a Combination Stone directly in your backpack. Double-click the Magi Stone and Amplifier Stone to select them, then double-click the Combination Stone and target a weapon you possess.

One of each stone is consumed on a successful enchantment. A weapon can carry one stone enchantment; the process rejects an already enchanted weapon. The Magi Stone chooses Poison, Lightning or Flamestrike.

Combination Stones have a usable definition, but no acquisition route is specified in the active drop or crafting tables. Check the currently available shard shops or rewards before planning an enchantment.

sections.title: Stone drop rates
paragraphs: Drops exclude owned, pet, summoned and invulnerable creatures. Ratings refer to the creature’s current difficulty score.

Magi Stones drop from difficulty 80 or higher at a 1-in-750 chance. The three effects are chosen equally after a successful drop. Amplifier Stones drop from difficulty 40–69 at a 1-in-250 chance, then select Lesser, Medium or Greater with 70%, 25% and 5% probabilities. Difficulty 70–79 does not qualify for either stone group.

sections.title: How the effect works
paragraphs: The effect is applied immediately on a successful hit; it is not a separate cast that movement can interrupt. Spell strength feeds the chosen spell’s effect calculation and does not mean that much guaranteed damage. Poison has its own duration and resistance behavior. Use the spell reference for Lightning and Flamestrike calculations.

articles.title: Creatures, monsters & the bestiary
articles.summary: Compare every loaded creature definition, its combat statistics, stored resistance properties, taming rating and declared rewards.
articles.keywords: bestiary monster creature animal vendor boss stats health armor damage physical fire cold poison energy resistance spell skill taming loot spawn

sections.title: Use the complete catalogue
paragraphs: The bestiary covers 1,147 loaded creature definitions: ordinary wildlife, dungeon enemies, named encounters, custom monsters, mounts, companions and town NPCs. Search by name or family, then review health, damage, armor, stored resistance properties, skills and taming ratings.

A loaded definition is available to the server, but that alone does not establish a current spawn location or schedule. Spawn-group membership describes a possible encounter mix. It does not mean every member appears everywhere that group is used.
Different definitions can share the same displayed name. Ore colors, vendors of different races and custom versions remain separate entries so their statistics and behavior are not mixed together.

sections.title: Read creature statistics
paragraphs: Ranges are values randomized at creation. Expressions and conditional values are retained where the scripts do not give a single fixed number. A blank statistic means that the definition does not explicitly set it; the creature can receive a native default or a value from the actual spawn.

Health, strength, damage and armor describe different parts of an encounter. The catalogue also records stored physical, fire, cold, poison and energy resistance properties. Percentage-based elemental resistance reduction is disabled in the current combat configuration, so those stored percentages are not current damage-reduction promises. Native fire-immunity flags are separate.

The skill list records configured skills. A Magery value alone does not promise a particular cast sequence. Where a creature explicitly adds spells, its repertoire is listed. Additional scripted attacks and reactive effects appear in its ability notes.

sections.title: Compare difficulty
paragraphs: Many combat creatures have a configured base rating on a 1–100 scale. Use .difficulty and target an NPC on your facet within 24 tiles to inspect its current rating in game.

The rating informs experience and reward scaling. It is not a suggested player level, a promise of soloability, or a replacement for checking attacks and resistances. A low-health caster, dismounting enemy or summoning encounter can still threaten an unsuitable build.
Civilian treatment takes precedence over ordinary combat scoring. Uncatalogued creatures use a runtime value rather than an invented wiki tier.

sections.title: Read rewards correctly
paragraphs: Death loot lists items and pools declared for corpse creation. A random pool or chance-based entry is a possible reward. Multiple entries can produce multiple selections; a single weighted selection chooses among its alternatives.

Carving resources are a separate category: meat, hides, feathers and other materials associated with the corpse. Carried equipment is also separate, since protected or otherwise restricted equipment may not become player loot.

Eligible wild enemies can additionally receive centrally scaled gold and a difficulty-based treasure-map roll. Their own item pools and retained custom currency entries remain separate from that reward.

General random armor and weapon rewards use classic equipment pools. Specifically named custom rewards and craftable equipment remain separate; the presence of an item definition does not put it into general monster loot.

sections.title: What the catalogue establishes
paragraphs: The catalogue was refreshed against the development scripts on 9 October 2026. It includes the new town quest contacts, three temporary Necromancy summons, Roper, Mimic and the additional rideable Owlbear; 29 retired creature definitions have been removed. World placement and runtime activation are separate from this reference list.

articles.title: Monster difficulty & reward scaling
articles.summary: Understand difficulty ratings, scaled gold, treasure-map chances and the difference between loot and carving.
articles.keywords: difficulty gold reward monster purse treasure map drop chance corpse carving hide loot tier experience

sections.title: How the rating is used
paragraphs: The configured scale runs from 1 to 100. The base catalogue combines the creature’s listed health, strongest combat skills and taming rating into a fixed score. Current scoring gives civilians special treatment and falls back to a live creature value where no base entry exists.
Inspect a nearby NPC with .difficulty. Its current score is the reference for difficulty-based rewards; the number is not a recommended character level.

Changing a pet’s level does not automatically make killing that owned pet a valid reward source. Player characters, pets, summons, owned creatures and invulnerable NPCs are excluded from the relevant wild-enemy reward paths.

sections.title: Scaled gold
paragraphs: Only creatures marked eligible for central gold receive this purse. The core amount is difficulty squared divided by four, rounded down, then adjusted by the configured band multiplier. Each stage uses whole gold pieces. The final roll is 80–120% of that amount, with a minimum of 1 and maximum of 5,000 gold.

The payout is added once to a valid corpse. It does not erase money the creature already carried, and it does not replace a retained custom gold declaration. Town civilians and controlled or summoned creatures do not qualify for this central wild-enemy purse.

tables.caption: Central gold only; additional declared loot is separate.

sections.title: Treasure-map rolls
paragraphs: Eligible wild combat NPCs have a separate map roll when their corpse is created. Difficulty selects the map level, and higher-level maps have a lower drop probability.

Civilian NPCs, guards, pets, summons, owned creatures and invulnerable creatures do not qualify. Animal- and human-brained NPCs must also have negative karma; harmless wildlife and ordinary townsfolk are not map sources.

sections.title: Items and rare selections
paragraphs: The creature’s death-loot declarations determine its item pools, quantities and chances. A one-in-N roll applies to that declaration; it does not guarantee one reward after N kills.
Shared loot pools can be used by several enemies. Their configured entries were balanced directly. The central gold multiplier is not an additional universal multiplier for rare-item chances.
Some custom creatures retain explicit currency or map entries of their own. Check the individual bestiary entry as well as this central scaling guide.

sections.title: Carving and carried equipment
paragraphs: Treat carving materials separately from ordinary death loot. A resource such as hides or meat belongs to the corpse’s carving configuration. Even a currency-like resource declared there should not be read as a guaranteed purse on death.

Carried equipment can have protection or other restrictions. Ambient Order and Chaos patrol equipment, for example, is not intended as player loot. The bestiary keeps equipment separate from declared death rewards.

sections.title: Recipe scrolls and general equipment
paragraphs: Eligible hostile monster corpses with a difficulty rating of 81–100 have a 2% recipe-scroll roll. Players, pets, summons and protected characters are excluded; the Custom recipes guide explains the other acquisition routes.
General random armor and weapon selections now use classic equipment. Explicit custom rewards and crafting materials are separate from those pools.

sections.title: Tame an eligible creature
paragraphs: Use Animal Taming and select a creature you can see. The current native fallback range is 10 tiles. The process uses several taming attempts and the configured Taming skill checks; a listed taming rating is not a guaranteed success threshold.

Normal taming rejects player characters, your own character, already-controlled pets, creatures with zero Taming, creatures with positive Animal Lore and human, elf or gargoyle player-body NPCs. A positive Taming value therefore needs to be read alongside those eligibility rules.
Attacking the creature before taming it can make the native taming attempt harder. When taming succeeds, the creature becomes owned and begins following the tamer.

Use the bestiary to compare active abilities, base statistics and food needs before choosing a pet. Current combat does not apply percentage reduction from the stored elemental-resistance properties. A mount’s taming rating does not by itself prove that a particular acquisition route is available in the world.

sections.title: Common pet commands
paragraphs: Address your owned pet by name, or use the client’s all-pets speech forms where supported. Some commands open a target cursor. Ownership and command eligibility are checked again when the target is selected.
Berserk-brained creatures do not accept ordinary player commands. Summoned creatures remain controlled by their summoner. Dead bonded pets cannot attack, guard, transfer or drop items.

sections.title: Feed according to species
paragraphs: The bestiary lists each definition’s food configuration where it is specified: examples include raw meat, crops, fruit, grain, grass or prepared food. Offer appropriate food rather than assuming every pet eats the same items.

The deployed global food-decay interval is 24 real-world hours, with individual definitions able to override or disable it. The current configuration does not enable hunger damage; generic advice that a pet automatically dies or deserts from starvation is not established for this shard.
Food needs and maximum food differ by species. Some untameable custom monsters have food disabled entirely. Native animal behavior can also search for suitable food.

sections.title: Treat an injured pet
paragraphs: Veterinary is the configured animal-treatment skill used with bandages. Its listed delay is 2 seconds; the actual treatment still follows native range, eligibility and skill rules.

Animal Lore, Taming and Veterinary also contribute to normal stable capacity. Pet progression raises maximum resource pools but does not eliminate the need to heal, cure or manage an injured companion.

sections.title: Stable and retrieve pets
paragraphs: At an animal trainer, use the stable speech interaction and target a pet you own. The trainer must see it. Summoned creatures cannot be stabled, and the pet’s backpack must be empty before storage.

Use the trainer’s retrieve interaction to claim stored pets. Native storage represents the existing creature as a figurine; the retrieval path restores that creature rather than advertising a new trained pet.

Without a trainer-specific override, base storage capacity depends on your combined adjusted Taming, Animal Lore and Veterinary. Each of those skills at 100.0 or higher adds one slot per full skill point above 90.0. For example, three skills at 100.0 add 30 slots to the base capacity of 5. Trainer overrides and the server container limit can still constrain storage.

sections.title: Control capacity and bonding
paragraphs: Species follower-slot values are included in the catalogue, but the native AOS follower-slot cap is not enabled by the deployed configuration. A universal five-slot active-pet rule should therefore not be assumed from those values.

The loaded scripts do not establish a general player bonding quest or timed bonding process. Some ambient NPCs are explicitly bonded for their own behavior; that does not make the same rule available to every player pet.

sections.title: Configured companion types
paragraphs: These custom definitions are loaded alongside ordinary tameable creatures. Their presence in the catalogue does not establish a vendor, quest, spawn location or guaranteed player acquisition route.
Where the creature becomes a normal owned pet, the generic pet-progression rules still apply. Its special behavior is separate from the level 10 and level 20 perk choices.

sections.title: Succubus companion
paragraphs: The custom Succubus companion is a small caster pet with configured Taming 99.0, health 15–27 and Magery 60.1–80.0. Its owner-healing routine is attached specifically to this companion definition.

It checks every 5 seconds. If either it or its owner is fighting, the owner is injured, both are within 5 tiles with line of sight, the pet has at least 10 mana and the healing cooldown has expired, it restores 10% of the owner’s maximum health, rounded down with a minimum of 1. Healing cannot exceed maximum health.
Each successful heal costs 10 pet mana and starts a 10-second cooldown. An idle or temporarily unowned companion continues its checks so that it can heal later when the conditions are met.

sections.title: Cerberus companion
paragraphs: The custom Cerberus companion has configured Taming 80.0, health 190–227 and strength 120–149. Its stored physical-resistance property is 50–70; current combat does not activate percentage-based elemental resistance reduction. Its Wrestling and Tactics are approximately 80–89.
The owner-healing timer is not attached to Cerberus. The fact that both companions appear in the same set does not give it the Succubus healing ability.

sections.title: Owlbear mount
paragraphs: The custom Owlbear mount has configured Taming 50.0, strength 100, dexterity 50 and intelligence 25. Its melee damage is 5–10 with armor 10, Wrestling 50.0 and Tactics 50.0.

It accepts raw meat and has maximum food 20. Its definition includes the mount and figurine resources required for native riding and shrinking. The Owlbear mount is separate from a Druid’s Owlbear Shape talent.

sections.title: Additional rideable Owlbear
paragraphs: The additional Owlbear mount is a separate definition with Taming 50.0, Strength 100, Dexterity 50, Intelligence 25, damage 5–10, armor 10, Wrestling 50.0 and Tactics 50.0. Its maximum health is not explicitly set.

This version accepts fruit, grain and grass and has a food capacity of 20. It has its own riding memory and shrink figurine. The original meat-eating Owlbear and the Druid’s Owlbear Shape remain separate. The definition alone does not establish a purchase or spawn location.

Mytheril and Mithril are separate configured material names. Legacy ore-ride definitions are also retained for compatibility, but they are not additional entries in this 124-combination whistle selection.

sections.title: Rare mount appearances
paragraphs: The loaded rare-mount system can place one random color-and-species mount with its matching reusable whistle at a configured spawner. The interval for each such spawner is 14 real-world days.

This is a per-spawner interval, not a claim that a mount appears at every location or that the world has any particular number of these spawners. The source does not establish public coordinates for this guide.

sections.title: Use a mount whistle
paragraphs: Put the whistle in your own carried inventory and double-click it while unmounted. A valid whistle is attuned to a specific species and color.

On a successful eligible use, it binds to the rider. It brings its existing living mount nearby and attempts to mount the rider, or creates the matching mount if the former linked creature is no longer available. A linked creature owned by somebody else cannot be claimed through the whistle.

A bound whistle cannot be used by another rider. It is reusable rather than a one-use consumable, but the scripts do not promise that a replacement creature preserves the prior creature’s pet experience or special choices.

sections.title: Training and ownership
paragraphs: The individual mount has ordinary ownership and pet-progression behavior where eligible. A material-colored mount does not bypass the ownership-reset rule for trained pets.
Keep the rider binding of the whistle separate from the current ownership of the creature. The interaction rechecks both before bringing an existing mount to the rider.
